definitions.balls: legal deliveries in the window; wides and no-balls are dropped, with anything that happened on them
definitions.caught: wicket_kind == 'caught', every catch by a fielder (caught and bowled is a separate kind, not counted)
definitions.caught_keeper: the 'caught' dismissals whose fielder is the innings' wicketkeeper by the proxy in cordon_proxy
definitions.other_dismissals: lbw, run out, stumped, caught and bowled, hit wicket and the rest: outside the model (ADR-007), so not wickets here, though their balls count
definitions.runs_batter: runs off the bat on legal deliveries

cordon_proxy.method: Cricsheet does not label fielding positions. A wicketkeeper is recognised only through stumpings: a 'known keeper' is any fielder credited with a stumping anywhere in the men's Test archive. In each innings at most one known keeper is taken to be keeping: of those with a catch or stumping in that innings, the one with most stumpings in the match, then most dismissals in the match, then most stumpings in the archive. A 'caught' dismissal by that fielder is a keeper catch.
cordon_proxy.quality: Keeper catches are a lower bound on cordon catches, because slips and gully cannot be identified at all; all catches are the upper bound. Measured, in archive_counts: where two known keepers caught in the same innings only one can have been keeping, so the rule keeps one and rejects the rest (rejected_as_second_keeper_in_innings); which of the two it keeps is a judgement by the ranking above, not an observation. Not measurable from this data: a known keeper fielding elsewhere is counted wrongly when no other known keeper caught in that innings, and a keeper with no stumping in the archive is missed. The split was not checked against an external source.
